items.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: And then of course there had been jazz musicians like Sidney Bechet and Tommy Ladnier and Lord Hopkins. They’d been to Europe with different groups and shows and things like that.

ctx.x: Do you think it was necessary for England and actually some of the United States to be introduced to jazz through the white bands first? And then start to be able to accept what Ellington and some— © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

Well jazz hadn’t sort of — jazz had been a novelty rather in Europe. But once you got into the 30s, you had these big ones coming, Fats Waller here, and Duke and I remember Lunceford came before World War II. I missed him. Calloway, Cab Calloway I think toured. And then of course there had been jazz musicians like Sidney Bechet and Tommy Ladnier and Lord Hopkins. They’d been to Europe with different groups and shows and things like that. But when I got to New York in ‘37, I’d been writing for the French magazine,…
Did you have aspirations to be a writer before you got into the music?
